title: One agent ask for a Google secret through Hubs
lede: The agent holds only a Privilege agent access key. It asks the Hubs gateway over MCP for a Google Secret Manager secret; the gateway's policy decides, and on an allow the custodian releases the secret. An out-of-scope ask is refused — the refusal is the product.

nodes.label: AI agent
sub: holds only an agent access key

nodes.label: Agent access key
sub: the only credential the agent has

nodes.label: Custodian
sub: releases the secret on an ALLOW only

nodes.label: Gateway Policy Denied
sub: out-of-scope ask: refusal is the product

steps.title: The agent asks
steps.what: The agent calls MCP tools/call get_google_secret with the secret name, carrying its Privilege agent access key. It holds no Google credential at any point.

steps.title: The key identifies the agent
steps.what: The gateway recognises the agent by its key. The key opens nothing by itself: it is an identity, not a Google credential.

steps.title: The policy evaluates
steps.what: The gateway's policy checks the key's per-secret grant. This agent's grant lists projects/demo/secrets/google-agent-credential and nothing else.

steps.title: In scope: allow, custodian releases
steps.what: On an allow the Hubs custodian reads the secret from the (mock) Google Secret Manager and releases it into the agent session. The display masks it and labels it MOCK (rule 4 exception: a mock-issued credential may be shown).

steps.title: Out of scope: the refusal is the product
steps.what: Ask for the billing secret with the same key and the policy refuses: Gateway Policy Denied. The secret never left the custodian, and the refusal is recorded with the agent's identity.
